nodes.name: Impregnation and thermal decomposition
nodes.procedure: The Ni(OH)2/C catalyst was synthesized by impregnation of Vulcan XC-72 carbon black support (160 mg) with an ethanol solution (600 μL ultrapure water and 200 μL ethanol) and 0.68 mL of 1.0 M Ni(NO3)2 at a nominal metal loading of 20 wt.%. The mixture was sonicated for 2 min and then magnetically stirred for 24 h. Finally, after 12 h of freeze drying, the obtained powder material was placed in a muffle furnace and heated in air at 200 °C for 2 h.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe co-impregnation
nodes.procedure: The Ni–Fe layered double hydroxide (Ni–Fe/C) catalyst was prepared by a similar method as the Ni(OH)2/C catalyst, except that a mixture of 1.0 M Ni(NO3)2 (2.7 mL) and 1.0 M Fe(NO3)3 (0.9 mL) with a Ni/Fe molar ratio of 3:1 was added together with 836 mg Vulcan XC-72 carbon black support in the impregnation solution (1 mL absolute ethanol and 400 μL ultrapure water). [Includes same sonication (2 min), stirring (24 h), freeze drying (12 h), and calcination (200°C, 2 h) as Ni(OH)2/C synthesis]

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2/C exhibits α-Ni(OH)2 phase (pdf#00-038-0715) with characteristic (003) and (006) diffraction peaks; after solvothermal treatment and OER test, transforms to β-Ni(OH)2-like phase (pdf#00-014-0117) with (001) peak shift and broadening.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared catalyst exhibits an α×Ni(OH)2 phase (pdf#00-038-0715) based on X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis (Fig. 1a for samples sprayed on carbon paper electrodes, and Supplementary Fig. 1a for powder samples) according to the characteristic (003) and (006) diffraction peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)2/C shows nanosheet morphology with ~10 nm lateral size after OER test; Ni(OH)2/C-120 shows larger lateral sizes 50-500 nm with majority interlayer distance decreased from 0.67 to 0.48 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A nanosheet morphology was revealed by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) (Supplementary Figs. 1b, c)... leading to significantly larger lateral sizes ranging from 50 to 500 nm (Supplementary Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: DEMS reveals cathodic O2 evolution during NiOOH reduction starting ~1.38 V vs RHE for Ni(OH)2/C (amount correlates with Ni oxidation extent), nearly absent for Ni(OH)2/C-120 and Fe-Ni(OH)2/C; 18O-labeling shows substantial surface LOM (m/z=34 signal) for Ni(OH)2/C but lower for Ni(OH)2/C-120 and Ni-Fe/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Reversing the electrode potential to 1.5 V, the DEMS signal of evolved O2 gradually decreases and disappeared. Unexpectedly, when further lowering the electrode potential to 1.38 V, O2 evolution emerges in the DEMS signal again... The Ni(OH)2/C-120 catalyst with a significantly lower Ni(OH)2/NiOOH redox activity shows nearly no DEMS signal of the cathodic OER (Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Potential-dependent in situ Raman shows NiOOH Ni-O modes at 474 cm⁻¹ (e_g bending δ(Ni^{III}-O)) and 555 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g} stretching ν(Ni^{III}-O)) appearing at 1.38 V, intensifying above; NiOO⁻ superoxo (O-O) band 850-1200 cm⁻¹ appears at 1.42 V for Ni(OH)2/C (before anodic OER at 1.56 V); NiOO⁻ signal attenuates during cathodic scan correlating with cathodic OER; weaker NiOO⁻ on Ni(OH)2/C-120 requiring higher potential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the oxidation of Ni(OH)2 starts at 1.38 V, two Raman bands appear at 474 and 555 cm^{-1}, designated as the e_g bending (marked as δ(Ni^{III}-O)) and A_{1g} stretching (marked as ν(Ni^{III}-O)) vibrational modes of Ni–O in the NiOOH active phase... a broad Raman band is observed between 850-1200 cm^{-1} at potentials above 1.42 V, which has been designated to the superoxo (O–O) vibration of negatively charged NiOO⁻ species.
